en: Storm surges can flood coastal areas, so families in low-lying zones like Tacloban must evacuate to higher ground before a typhoon hits.
Floodwater mixed with soil can carry leptospirosis bacteria, so you should always wash your feet with soap after wading in muddy rain floods.
Volcanic ash from Mayon Volcano contains tiny rock particles that can damage lungs, so wearing an N95 mask protects your health during an eruption.
Stagnant water in the water cycle creates breeding grounds for mosquitoes, so emptying unused tires and cans prevents dengue fever in your neighborhood.
The Sun emits ultraviolet radiation that causes sunburns, so applying sunscreen and wearing a hat protects your skin during outdoor recess.
During an earthquake, dropping to the ground and hiding under a sturdy table protects you from falling ceiling materials in your classroom.
High humidity in a tropical climate makes sweat evaporate slower, so drinking plenty of water prevents heat exhaustion during outdoor sports.
If you get lost at night, you can use the North Star, Polaris, to find true north and navigate your way back safely.
A full moon causes stronger gravitational pull that creates higher high tides, so avoid playing on rocky beaches during these king tides.
Heavy rain saturates soil on steep slopes like in Baguio, increasing landslide risks, so residents must evacuate when local officials issue warnings.
Sand and gravel rocks act as natural filters in the ground, removing harmful dirt from rainwater to help provide clean drinking water.
Tall objects like trees attract lightning strikes during thunderstorms, so you should immediately seek shelter inside a fully enclosed building to stay safe.
